finance_aml.gbm.baseline_gap_note: This reaches minority-class F1 well below the published 0.6323. Two differences account for most of it and both are deliberate. (1) The published baseline uses IBM's Graph Feature Preprocessor, which ships in `snapml` under a Proprietary licence and is therefore excluded by this project's commercial-OK-only rule; what is reimplemented here is the documented typology set (degree, fan-in/out, reciprocity, k-hop cycle closure, burst degree, scatter-gather). (2) The corpus injects CYCLE attempts of up to 10 hops (HI-Small_Patterns.txt), while reachability here is computed to 4 hops because the boolean sparse powers grow quickly beyond that. The evaluation is also strictly inductive: graph aggregates are fitted on the training window only, so no test-time edge informs a training-time feature. Reported as measured; not adjusted to close the gap.

satellite_comms.telemanom.dataset: ESA Anomaly Dataset (ESA-ADB), Mission1 lightweight channels 41-46
satellite_comms.telemanom.metric_note: Event-wise F-beta at beta=0.5 under the overlap rule, which is what ESA-ADB and Telemanom report. Telemanom's widely-quoted 0.71 is F0.5, not F1. point_adjusted_f1 is shown only to expose how much point adjustment inflates: TSB-AD (NeurIPS 2024) found a uniform random score ranks 26th of 32 detectors under it. Only labels whose ESA-ADB Category is 'Anomaly' count as positives; the 690 annotated rare *nominal* events do not.

telecom_ids.qml.framing: Architecture comparison, not a performance claim. The data is synthetic because no commercial-OK real attack corpus exists. Every published QML-IDS figure we could verify sits below a random forest on the same data, and arXiv:2512.05069 was withdrawn by its own authors for insufficient evaluation. Per-class F1 is the headline; aggregate accuracy is shown beside it because Engelen et al. (WTMC 2021) demonstrated it stays at 0.99 across a label correction that moved Bot F1 from 0.60 to 0.99.
